summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored Canadian documents on the federal Immigrant Investor Program (IIP), the Immigrant Investor Venture Capital (IIVC) pilot and the Quebec Investor Program: the 2014 CIC evaluation of the federal Business Immigration Program, Budget 2014 and the Economic Action Plan 2014 Act, the Jia FCA judgment, the IIVC ministerial instructions and IRCC notices, six Quebec ministerial orders, the 2018 draft and 2023 amending Quebec regulations, an Investissement Québec access-to-information reply, IRCC Facts & Figures 2015 tables and the two IRCC open-data workbooks (admissions by citizenship and by province, 2015 to July 2026). Added every Investor-class cell of the evaluation tables (profile, costs, acceptance rates, processing times, IMDB/CEEDD income and business tables, capital raised, provincial allocations, out-migration), every yearly and every non-zero monthly/quarterly Investor cell of the IRCC workbooks for 114 citizenships and four provinces, Investor shares of all permanent residents 2006-2015, the budgeted termination cost, rules (IIVC fees and net worth, Quebec net worth and stay requirements) and dated events. The stored evaluation lacks chapters 2, 3, 6 and the appendices, and monthly/quarterly cells printed 0 in the IRCC workbooks were not written as rows; both are marked partial.

program_terms.location: Canada Gazette Part I, 24 Jan 2015, Ministerial Instructions Respecting the Immigrant Investor Venture Capital Class, s. 8(a)
program_terms.quote: in respect of a principal applicant, $1,050
program_terms.notes: Processing fee for a permanent resident visa application in the IIVC class. Printed "$" in a federal instrument (Canadian dollars). Valid_to is the last intake day (instructions had effect to 27 Jan 2020).

program_terms.applies_to: spouse or common-law partner of the principal applicant
program_terms.location: Canada Gazette Part I, 24 Jan 2015, Ministerial Instructions Respecting the Immigrant Investor Venture Capital Class, s. 8(b)
program_terms.quote: in respect of the spouse or common-law partner of the principal applicant, $550

program_terms.location: Canada Gazette Part I, 24 Jan 2015, Ministerial Instructions Respecting the Immigrant Investor Venture Capital Class, s. 8(c)
program_terms.quote: in respect of each family member of the principal applicant who is a dependent child, $150

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant (with spouse or common-law partner; primary residence excluded); lawfully acquired through business or investment activity
program_terms.location: Canada Gazette Part I, 24 Jan 2015, Ministerial Instructions Respecting the Immigrant Investor Venture Capital Class, s. 2(2)(a) and s. 1(1) "net worth"
program_terms.quote: have a net worth of at least $10,000,000 that they have lawfully acquired through business or investment activity
program_terms.notes: Plus: language benchmark CLB 5 in all four skills, and either a Canadian (or equivalent) post-secondary credential of at least one year or a net worth of at least $50,000,000 (s. 2(2)(b)-(c)); due diligence report from one of six designated firms; the $2,000,000 payment must be made within 75 days of the Minister's request or the application is refused (s. 6); must intend to reside outside Quebec.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant without a qualifying post-secondary credential (alternative to the education requirement)
program_terms.location: Canada Gazette Part I, 24 Jan 2015, Ministerial Instructions Respecting the Immigrant Investor Venture Capital Class, s. 2(2)(c)
program_terms.quote: have a net worth, lawfully acquired through business or investment activity, of at least $50,000,000, or have one of the following
program_terms.notes: Alternative to the education requirement; the $10,000,000 net worth and $2,000,000 payment still apply.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant with spouse or common-law partner if included; lawful origin; donations received in the 6 months before the application excluded
program_terms.location: Gazette officielle du Québec 8 novembre 2023, p. 4962-4963, art. 13 replacing RIQ art. 37 para. 2
program_terms.quote: d’un avoir net dont l’origine licite doit être démontrée et d’au moins 2 000 000 $
program_terms.notes: Other conditions from 1 Jan 2024: 2 years of management experience in the 5 years before applying (outside ineligible sectors, which include real estate, Annexe E); secondary diploma; oral French level 7; placement and contribution within 120 days of the Minister's request; work permit (IRPR 204(c)); stays (next row). Applications filed before 1 Jan 2024 are decided under the old rules (art. 118.12). Printed "$" in a Quebec regulation (Canadian dollars).

program_terms.applies_to: investor: one stay of at least 6 months in Quebec within 2 years of the work permit; the investor or the included spouse/partner: another stay of at least 6 months
program_terms.location: Gazette officielle du Québec 8 novembre 2023, p. 4962-4963, art. 13 replacing RIQ art. 37 para. 7
program_terms.quote: le ressortissant étranger a séjourné au Québec pour une période d’au moins 6 mois et lui ou son époux ou conjoint de fait inclus dans la demande a séjourné au Québec pour une autre période d’au moins 6 mois
program_terms.notes: Selection condition, met before permanent selection.

program_terms.applies_to: main applicant alone or with accompanying spouse/partner; lawful origin; donations received in the 6 months before the application excluded
program_terms.location: Gazette officielle du Québec 28 mars 2018, p. 1989 (PDF p. 9), draft art. 38(2) and art. 39
program_terms.quote: d’un avoir net d’au moins 2 000 000 $ dont l’origine licite doit être démontrée
program_terms.notes: From the DRAFT regulation (same caveat as the 1,200,000 $ placement row from this source): the final regulation (décret 963-2018) in force 2 Aug 2018 is not stored. Also: management experience, pass mark on the selection grid, placement within 120 days of the notice of intent, 5-year irrevocable term; financial intermediaries registered with the AMF, head office in Quebec, 3 years in operation.

events.title: Quebec decision on receipt of investor and other economic applications (AM 2017-004)
events.description: Ministerial order AM 2017-004 of 24 March 2017 (Gazette officielle 30 March 2017) set a decision on the receipt and processing of selection certificate applications in the skilled worker, investor, self-employed and entrepreneur subcategories; it ended on 31 March 2018 (the 2017 caps are not given in this document).

events.title: IRCC removes the venture capital investor pilot from its instructions
events.description: IRCC announced that the IIVC pilot is closed, that applications stopped being accepted on 30 December 2015, and that the programme instructions are removed because the last applications in processing have been finalised.
events.quote: The IIVC program information in our instructions will be removed as the last applications that were being processed have now been finalized.

events.title: Second intake for the venture capital investor pilot
events.description: Under Ministerial Instructions MI18, IRCC accepted IIVC applications from 13 February to 15 April 2015 (after the first window of 28 Jan-11 Feb 2015 under MI17).
events.quote: Through MI17 and M18, IRCC also accepted applications from January 28 to February 11, 2015 as well as from February 13 to April 15, 2015.

new_indicators.name: Average characteristic of programme migrants
new_indicators.definition: Average (mean) of a characteristic of people admitted through a programme or of their businesses, other than income (e.g. years of prior business experience, businesses owned, ownership share, personal income tax paid), as printed by the source; category= says what is averaged and unit gives its unit. Never calculated by us.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-can1 for the CIC 2014 evaluation of the federal Business Immigration Program (survey and IMDB averages for Investor class immigrants).

new_indicators.name: Programme share of a combined budget or cost
new_indicators.definition: Percentage of the costs of a wider government programme or budget line attributable to the investor programme or class, in a period, as printed. Never calculated by us.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-can1 for the CIC 2014 BIP evaluation (Investor class 56.6% of BIP costs 2006/07-2011/12).

new_indicators.name: Implied annual cost of investor capital
new_indicators.definition: Annual rate (percent per year) at which a government or fund receiving investor-programme capital effectively pays for it (e.g. commissions on interest-free loans expressed as compound interest), as estimated by the source.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-can1 for the CIC 2014 evaluation (federal IIP commissions equivalent to about 1.5% / 1.1% a year).

new_indicators.name: Investor-programme funds allocated to regional funds
new_indicators.definition: Money raised by a government-run investor programme that is allocated or transferred to regional (provincial, territorial) funds in a period, and amounts those funds placed in a stated use (category=), as printed. Use breakdown destination= for the region.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-can1 for Table 5.8 of the CIC 2014 evaluation (federal IIP allocations by province 2007-2011).

new_indicators.name: Application grant rate
new_indicators.definition: Grants as a percentage of decisions or of all finalisations (grants, refusals and withdrawals) in a period, as printed by the source; notes give the base. Never calculated by us. Companion to cbi_rejection_rate and withdrawal_rate.
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-aus2; reused by extract-cbi-can1 for the acceptance rates in Table 4.2 of the CIC 2014 evaluation.

new_indicators.name: Income of programme migrants
new_indicators.definition: Typical annual income (average, median or approximate, as the source states) of people admitted through a programme, in a period, as printed. Use breakdown applicant= and category= for the group (e.g. age band).
new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-cbi-aus2; reused by extract-cbi-can1 for IMDB incomes of Investor class immigrants (CIC 2014 evaluation).

ledger.contains: CIC Evaluation Division, Evaluation of the Federal Business Immigration Program (June 2014), as stored: summary page, executive summary and chapters 1, 4, 5 and 7 only (chapters 2, 3, 6 and Appendices A-F are not in the stored file). Covers the Entrepreneur, Self-employed and Investor classes 2007-2011. Taken for the Investor class (IN): rules and thresholds (already in rules), admissions and shares of business immigrants (Table 1.2/4.3), profile at admission (Table 1.3), survey profile, costs by fiscal year (Table 1.4) and cost share, applications/decisions/acceptance rate/processed (Table 4.2), inventory (Figure 4.1, already in), 80% processing times (Table 4.3, with the conflicting 32/38-month text), survey satisfaction and help, all IN cells of the IMDB tables 5.1-5.3, 5.9-5.10, 5.12-5.18 and 5.21, CEEDD tables 5.4-5.6, survey Table 5.11 and business text figures, capital raised federal/Quebec/combined (Table 5.7), commissions, allocations by province with participation years (Table 5.8, added as events), active-investment shares, 10,781 FTEs, interprovincial tables 5.19-5.20. Not taken because they are not about the investor programme: EN/SE/federal-BI/Quebec-BI/FSW/PNP columns, Table 4.1 levels targets (all business classes, federal and Quebec), federal BIP inventory totals (24,967/24,976 cases, 82,832 persons), average BIP cost per application ($2,654). Printed checks: Table 4.2 IN processed = positive+negative+withdrawn for every year; Tables 5.5 and 5.6 IN parts sum to their totals and Table 5.8 shares sum to 100%, but the nine Table 5.8 amounts sum to 2,491,970,740, not the printed total 2,483,979,999 (difference 7,990,741); Table 1.3 IN shares round to 100. Conflicts noted in rows: Table 1.2 vs 4.3 IN share 2008 (81.3% vs 81.2%); Section 4.1.3 text (32 and 38 months) vs Table 4.3 (34 and 43). Net inventory impact row (received minus processed) quoted in notes, not taken as rows. Table 1.4 cost shares print 56.6+39.5+6.3=102.4%.
ledger.to_do: Chapters 2 (methodology), 3 (relevance), 6 (resource utilization: costs and cost per application by class) and Appendices A-F (incl. Table F-1/F-2 income profiles by class) are not in the stored copy; store them from the canada.ca evaluation pages and extract the Investor class figures.

ledger.contains: Federal Court of Appeal, Jia v. Canada (MCI), 2015 FCA 146 (A-320-14, with A-117-14), reasons delivered from the bench 15 June 2015: appeals seeking mandamus to force processing of federal Immigrant Investor Program applications are moot because IRPA s. 87.5 (in force 19 June 2014) terminated all IIP applications; appeals dismissed without costs. Appeal from Gleason J., 23 June 2014 (IMM-2621-13). Appendix A lists the appellants by Federal Court docket (numbered to 94; names not recorded under the dataset rules; the list length is not a programme statistic). The judgment event was already in the data; no numbers about the programme.

Budget 2014 (Economic Action Plan 2014, 11 Feb 2014), 428 pages. Investor content: Chapter 3.1 section "Immigrant Investor Program" (printed p. 81: proposal to end the federal Immigrant Investor and Entrepreneur programs, return applications and refund fees for applicants who applied on or before Budget Day, replace them with an Immigrant Investor Venture Capital Fund pilot; investors pay lower taxes; programme paused since July 2012) and the cost line in Table 3.1.1 (printed p. 82). The closure event was already in the data; this pass adds the budgeted cost (2 million, 2013-14, and total). The rest of the budget (tax, spending, other immigration measures) is out of scope.

Canada Gazette Part I, 24 Jan 2015: (1) Ministerial Instructions Respecting the Immigrant Investor Venture Capital Class (14 Jan 2015): net worth C$10 million (or C$50 million in place of the education requirement), CLB 5, education, C$2,000,000 non-guaranteed payment transferred to BDC for venture capital, 75-day payment deadline, processing fees $1,050/$550/$150, intent to reside outside Quebec, effective 28 Jan 2015 to 27 Jan 2020, schedule of six designated due diligence firms; (2) intake instructions: applications 28 Jan-11 Feb 2015 or until 500 received, random draw until 60 complete applications, up to 60 approvals ("Sixty is the maximum number of investments"). The C$2,000,000 term and the launch event were already in the data; this pass adds the fee and net worth rules. Caps (500 applications, 60 approvals) are kept in the launch event, not as observations. The rest of the issue (environment, spectrum, insurance, Bank of Canada balance sheet) is out of scope.

Quebec ministerial order AM 2018-001 (19 March 2018; Gazette 28 March 2018): suspends receipt of investor (and self-employed, entrepreneur) selection certificate applications 1 April-15 August 2018, caps skilled-worker applications at 5,000. Preamble: 2,409 investor applications awaiting processing on 1 Jan 2018 (already in the data), about 17,500 business-category persons awaiting permanent residence (all business programmes, not investor-only: not taken), skilled-worker and refugee figures (out of scope), and the earlier AM 2017-004 decision of 24 March 2017 (added as an event). The suspension event was already in the data.

Quebec ministerial order AM 2018-009 (10 July 2018; Gazette 1 Aug 2018), in force 2 Aug 2018-1 Apr 2019: Investor Program capped at 1,900 applications, at most 1,235 from China (incl. Hong Kong and Macao), receipt window 10 Sept 2018-15 March 2019, cap and window not applicable (and priority processing) for applicants with advanced intermediate French; also caps for entrepreneur (25/35), self-employed (50) and refugee sponsorship programmes (out of scope). Preamble: about 2,510 investor applications pending on 30 April 2018 (added), 19,285 business-programme persons awaiting permanent residence (all business programmes; not taken). Cap event already in the data; the caps are kept in that event.

Quebec ministerial order AM 2019-001 (4 Jan 2019; Gazette 16 Jan 2019): after the 2019 immigration plan, extends the Investor Program receipt period from 15 March to 31 August 2019 and the decision to 1 September 2019. No numbers; the event was already in the data.

Quebec ministerial order AM 2019-007 (22 Oct 2019; Gazette 30 Oct 2019): suspends receipt of Investor Program applications from 1 Nov 2019 to 1 July 2020, citing the government's wish to revise the programme; preamble recalls AM 2018-009, AM 2019-001 and AM 2019-003 (9 May 2019, added as an event). Also on the pages: other orders on skilled workers (AM 2019-006 end) and the self-employed programme (AM 2019-008), out of scope. No numbers; the suspension event was already in the data.

Quebec ministerial order 2020-001 (8 May 2020; Gazette 20 May 2020): keeps receipt of Investor Program applications suspended from 1 July 2020 to 1 April 2021, citing the government's wish to revise the programme. No numbers; the event was already in the data.

Quebec ministerial order 2021-007 (19 March 2021; Gazette 31 March 2021): keeps receipt of Investor Program applications suspended from 1 April 2021 to 1 April 2023. No numbers; the event was already in the data.

Décret 1570-2023 (25 Oct 2023; Gazette officielle du Québec 8 Nov 2023), Règlement modifiant le Règlement sur l'immigration au Québec. Investor content: art. 13 (new art. 37: management experience, net worth 2,000,000 $, diploma, oral French level 7, 5-year placement of 1,000,000 $ with IQ Immigrants Investisseurs plus 200,000 $ contribution within 120 days, work permit, two 6-month stays), arts. 14-21 (participating financial intermediaries: trust company or investment dealer authorised for 3 years with head office in Quebec; refunds within 30 days; contribution non-refundable except listed cases), art. 50 (offence), art. 56 (transitional art. 118.12), art. 59 (ineligible sectors incl. real estate), art. 61 (in force 1 Jan 2024). The placement, contribution and launch event were already in the data; this pass adds the net worth and stay rules. Other programmes in the decree (skilled workers, PEQ, self-employed, entrepreneurs, sponsorship) and the bingo decree on the same pages are out of scope.

Draft Règlement sur l'immigration au Québec (Gazette officielle du Québec 28 March 2018, 28 pages). Investor content: draft arts. 36-46 (investor definition, age 18+, management experience, net worth 2,000,000 $, 5-year placement of 1,200,000 $ with an Investissement Québec subsidiary through a financial intermediary, pass mark on the selection grid, intermediary conditions, 120-day placement deadline, refunds within 30 days), art. 113 (offence), art. 117 (transition for intermediaries), grid factor 2.3 (investor management experience in half-year steps, no points printed). The 1,200,000 $ term was already in the data; this pass adds the net worth rule. Other programmes (skilled workers, entrepreneurs, self-employed, family, refugees) out of scope.

Investissement Québec access-to-information response of 4 February 2026 (N/D 1-310-039): annex table of the value of refundable placements (loans) and non-refundable contributions by Quebec immigrant investors by fiscal year 2016-2017 to 2025-2026 (to 31 Dec 2025), in M$; note that the 200,000 $ non-refundable portion started 1 January 2024; cover letter and the notice of the right to review (p. 3, image, OCR-checked: legal text only). The 10 placement values and the 2024-25 and 2025-26 contributions were already in the data; this pass adds the printed 0 contribution for 2023-24. "N/A" cells (before the contribution existed) are not numbers and are not recorded.

IRCC Facts & Figures 2015 table "Canada - Permanent residents by category", 2006-2015 (all persons), numbers and percentage distribution for every immigration category. In scope: the Investor row (federal and Quebec combined). Investor admissions 2006-2015 were already in the data; this pass adds the Investor percentage of all permanent residents for each year. Other categories (skilled workers, family, refugees, entrepreneurs...) out of scope.

IRCC Facts & Figures 2015 table "Canada - Permanent residents by category (principal applicant)", 2006-2015, numbers and percentage distribution for every immigration category. In scope: the Investor row (federal and Quebec combined). Investor principal applicants 2006-2015 were already in the data; this pass adds the Investor share of all principal applicants for each year. Other categories out of scope. Investor numbers fall within the printed totals (e.g. 2,186 of 136,380 in 2006).

IRCC program delivery update of 29 January 2021: the IIVC class pilot is closed, applications stopped on 30 December 2015, instructions deleted because the last applications were finalised. No numbers. The 30 Dec 2015 closure event was already in the data; this pass adds the 29 Jan 2021 removal as its own event.

IRCC page on Ministerial Instructions 19 (issued 23 May 2015): IIVC applications accepted 25 May-30 Dec 2015; first 60 complete applications processed and up to 60 more on a waiting list; programme may close early once 60 investors approved or 60 in processing plus 60 waiting; earlier windows under MI17/MI18 (28 Jan-11 Feb and 13 Feb-15 Apr 2015). The MI19 event was already in the data; this pass adds the MI18 second-window event. The caps (60/60) are in the event descriptions, not observations.

IRCC open data workbook EN_ODP-PR-CitzImmCat (admissions of permanent residents by country of citizenship and immigration category, January 2015 to July 2026, monthly, quarterly and yearly). Only the Investor category is in scope (federal and Quebec investors combined; not split by programme). 114 countries/groups have an Investor row (including "Stateless"; "United Kingdom and Overseas Territories" mapped to GBR; "Palestinian Authority (Gaza/West Bank)" to PSE; "Hong Kong SAR" and "Macau SAR" kept separate from CHN). Taken: every yearly cell of every Investor row (including printed zeros) and every monthly and quarterly cell that is not a printed 0; "--" (1 to 4) recorded as a range 1-4. The 105 yearly rows already in the data were not repeated. All other categories (skilled workers, family, refugees, entrepreneurs, etc.) are out of scope. There is no all-countries Investor total row to check against; IRCC rounding means sums need not match the province table.
ledger.to_do: Monthly and quarterly cells printed as 0 were not written as rows (17907 cells); write them if the dataset wants explicit zero rows (decision needed). Everything else in scope is extracted.

ledger.contains: IRCC open data workbook EN_ODP-PR-ProvImmCat (admissions of permanent residents by province/territory of intended destination and immigration category, January 2015 to July 2026, monthly, quarterly, yearly). Investor rows exist for Quebec (Quebec Investor Program), Ontario, Alberta and British Columbia (federal programme tail); no Canada-wide Investor total. Taken: every yearly cell of the four Investor rows (including printed zeros after the federal cases ran out) and every monthly and quarterly cell that is not a printed 0; "--" recorded as 1-4. The 22 yearly rows already in the data were not repeated. Other categories are out of scope.
ledger.to_do: Monthly and quarterly cells printed as 0 were not written as rows (475 cells); write them if the dataset wants explicit zero rows (decision needed).

ledger.contains: Economic Action Plan 2014 Act, No. 1 (S.C. 2014, c. 20), full text. Investor content: Division 20 of Part 6, s. 303 adding IRPA s. 87.5 (termination of federal investor and entrepreneur applications not assessed before 11 Feb 2014; not applicable to Quebec-selected investors or applications with a final superior court determination before that date; fees and the investment returned without interest; provinces must return provincial allocations of terminated investments to the Minister; no recourse). The event was already in the data. No numbers about the programme; the rest of the Act (tax and other measures) is out of scope.
